That file contains `test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command` (lines 228-243), which asserts `rc != 0` when the reader closes. GITHUB FACTS show PR #9246 is open and unmerged, and its title says it fixes exactly this "closed-reader test" failure on ubuntu-26.04 runners. A second fix here would duplicate it and conflict with it, so this issue leaves the work to #9246. Per the pipeline-capability rule, the planner holds this issue on the blocked path until #9246 merges. The plan adds no steps that act on #9246 or PR #8960: no branch update, no re-run, no comments. The existing review and merge-base freshness automation brings #8960 up to date once `main` has the fix. C is rejected because the failure is deterministic on the uutils `cat` runner, not a flake.
Q2: This only applies if #9246 closes without merging. In that case, fix the root cause in `gh_retry` (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh`) and in every copy the contract tests check. Those are the inline `gh_retry() { ... }` copies in `review_autofix.yml` that `_inline_gh_retry` extracts (tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py:246-259), and `gh_retry_to_file` if it resends saved output the same way. After the fix, a closed reader gives a non-zero status no matter which `cat` the runner has. B is ruled out because the issue forbids loosening the test, and loosening it would hide undelivered output from production callers. C is ruled out because pinning the runner hides the defect without fixing it.
